body:
Science, education and regional cooperation came together in Kotor for the Third International Conference on Adriatic Biodiversity Protection — AdriBioPro2024, held from 1 to 4 October 2024.

Organised by the Institute of Marine Biology, University of Montenegro, the conference marked the University’s 50th anniversary and 25 years of the FAO AdriaMed project. Its programme connected aquatic biodiversity conservation with fisheries, aquaculture, climate change, environmental education and the sustainable development of the blue economy.

As Chair of the Conference, I participated in an event that brought researchers, policymakers and practitioners together to exchange knowledge across disciplines and borders. I also facilitated the SKILLS high-level panel, “Blue Economy in the South Adriatic Region,” guiding a discussion on aligning research, education and policy with regional skills and employment needs.

My scientific contribution included two posters co-authored with Mirjana Bartula: “Characteristics of aquarium Dubrovnik and Boka visits” and “Public understanding of Adriatic Sea biodiversity.” Both explored how understanding visitors and public perceptions can inform biodiversity education and the work of aquaria.

This gallery offers a visual record of the conference, its participants and the exchanges that connected marine science with policy and public engagement in Kotor.
